item.title: Port Allen begins its holiday celebration with Christmas tree lighting
item.description: PORT ALLEN - The city of Port Allen started their countdown to Christmas with a tree lighting on Wednesday night.Those with the city say people look forward to the event each year. Dozens gathered at the city's train depot to see lights and decorations.Port Allen's mayor, Terecita Pattan, said the event helps people get into the holiday spirit.Permalink| Comments

item.title: 'Mistletoe and Moss' held as part of Louisiana Lights on Tuesday night
item.description: BATON ROUGE - A special event known as "Mistletoe and Moss" was held at the Burden Museum and Gardens as part of the Louisiana Lights.Capital area vendors set up shop inside the light show to offer people the chance to get holiday shopping done.Louisiana Lights runs Wednesday through Sunday until Dec. 30.Permalink| Comments

item.title: BRFD: Unattended candle ignites curtains, causes total loss fire along Avenue J
item.description: BATON ROUGE &mdash; Investigators say an unattended candle caused a Thursday morning fire along Avenue J.&nbsp;Baton Rouge Fire officials said that firefighters arrived at the scene of the fire around 4:12 a.m. and got the blaze under control within 15 minutes.&nbsp;According to a BRFD spokesperson, two occupants made it safely outside, but the home is a total loss. item.title: Zachary Police Department hosting tree decorating contest at station; voting lasts through Dec. 22
item.description: ZACHARY &mdash; Zachary Police are getting into the holiday spirit and spreading Christmas cheer with a Christmas tree decorating contest.Community members are encouraged to visit the department to cast a vote for their favorite tree decorated by a local business.Voting extends through Dec. 22. Only one vote can be cast per person per day, unless you bring a toy to donate, then you get an extra vote.&nbsp;Permalink| Comments

item.title: WBRZ FLASHBACK: Downtown Baton Rouge saw multiple buildings torn down, changing skyline forever
item.description: BATON ROUGE &mdash; This week in WBRZ history, the downtown Baton Rouge skyline drastically changed when multiple buildings were imploded.&nbsp;On Dec. 13, 2003, the old Department of Insurance building that once stood right next to the State Capitol came down. item.title: Nominations open for Louisiana Wildlife Federation's 60th annual Conservation Achievement Awards
item.description: BATON ROUGE &mdash; Nominations for the Louisiana Wildlife Federation's 60th annual Conservation Achievement Awards have opened.The awards recognize individuals, businesses and organizations in Louisiana that have made outstanding contributions to the natural resource welfare and environmental quality of their community, parish and the state each year.Each honoree will receive a wildlife statuette and be honored at a banquet held in spring 2026.&nbsp;Nominations must be submitted via the LWF web
